- 
	-

const userStatus = 'active';

### <a id="_bookmark5"></a>Function names

- 
	- 
		- 
			- Use camelCase\.
			- Starting with a verb describing the action\.

Example:

const createUser = \(data\) => \{ \.\.\. \}; 

const deleteRoom = \(id\) => \{ \.\.\. \};

## Error Handling

• Use try\-catch blocks for database operations and asynchronous tasks\.  
• Return consistent JSON error objects to the frontend\.  
Example:

try \{

  const room = await Room\.findOne\(\{ code \}\);

  if \(\!room\) \{

    return \{ success: false, message: 'Room not found' \};

  \}

\} catch \(error\) \{

  console\.error\(error\);

  set\.status = 500;

  return \{ success: false, message: 'Internal server error' \};

\}

# CHAPTER 2\. REACT FRONTEND

## <a id="_bookmark16"></a>Vite \+ React Project Setup

Vite is used as the build tool for its superior speed and modern features\. The project was initialized using

npm create vite@latest

with the React\-TS template\.

 

__Key Libraries:__  
• __PixiJS__: For high\-performance 2D world rendering\.  
• __Tailwind CSS__: For sleek, glassmorphic UI design\.  
• __LiveKit SDK__: For real\-time spatial audio and video\.

## Component Architecture

We separate "Dumb" \(Presentational\) components from "Smart" \(Container\) components to improve modularity\.

- __Dumb Components: __Focus on UI rendering via props\.

Example Dumb Component:

const AvatarIcon = \(\{ url, name \}\) => \(

  <div className="rounded\-full border\-2 border\-primary overflow\-hidden">

    <img src=\{url\} alt=\{name\} />

  </div>

\);

- __Smart Components__: Manage state and business logic\.

Example Smart Component:

  


const RoomContainer = \(\) => \{

  const \[rooms, setRooms\] = useState\(\[\]\);

  useEffect\(\(\) => \{

    fetchRooms\(\)\.then\(setRooms\);

  \}, \[\]\);

  return <RoomList items=\{rooms\} />;

\};

## <a id="_bookmark19"></a>Code Style and Formatting

Consistency is maintained through naming conventions and styling rules\.

Example: <a id="_bookmark20"></a>

 \`RoomList\.tsx\`, \`useAuth\.ts\`, \`handleJoinRoom\(\)\`

## Class Convention

Use PascalCase for Typescript interfaces and components\.Example:

interface PlayerState \{

  x: number;

  y: number;

  isSitting: boolean;

\}

## <a id="_bookmark21"></a>Function Convention

• __API Calls__: Start with fetch or post \(e\.g\., fetchUserRooms\)\.  
• __Event Handlers__: Start with handle \(e\.g\., handleMovement\)\.

## <a id="_bookmark22"></a>Services and HTTP Requests

We use a centralized api\.ts utility to handle all fetch requests with standardized headers and error handling\.

Example:

export const apiFetch = async \(path: string, options = \{\}\) => \{

  const token = localStorage\.getItem\('token'\);

  const response = await fetch\(\`$\{BASE\_URL\}$\{path\}\`, \{

    \.\.\.options,

    headers: \{

      'Authorization': \`Bearer $\{token\}\`,

      'Content\-Type': 'application/json',

      \.\.\.options\.headers,

    \},

  \}\);

  return response\.json\(\);

\};

## <a id="_bookmark23"></a>Error Handling

Display user\-friendly notifications for API failures using a custom hook or global toast system\.

Example:<a id="_bookmark24"></a>

try \{

  await joinRoom\(code\);

\} catch \(err\) \{

  setError\("Invalid room code\. Please check and try again\."\);

\}

# CHAPTER 3\. API COMMUNICATION

## <a id="_bookmark26"></a>RESTful API Design

The platform follows RESTful principles for Dashboard operations \(CRUD\):  
• GET /api/rooms \- Fetch joined rooms\.  
• POST /api/rooms/join/:code \- Enter a workspace\.  
• GET /api/admin/stats \- Platform metrics\.

## Versioning

Currently, the API uses the /api prefix\. Future breaking changes will be introduced via /api/v1\.

## Security

• __JWT__: All protected routes require a Bearer token in the header\.  
• __Google OAuth__: One Tap tokens are verified server\-side\.  
• __Rate Limiting__: Applied to /api to prevent brute\-force attacks\.

<a id="_bookmark29"></a>

# CHAPTER 4\. MONGODB

## <a id="_bookmark30"></a>Requirement

Collection names use lowercase plural form \(e\.g\., users, rooms\)\. Each document has a unique \_id\. Relationships are managed via ObjectIDs and application\-level population\.

## Naming Conventions

1\. __\_id__: Standard MongoDB ObjectID format\.

2\. __Field Names__: Use camelCase\.  
Requirement: Field names must be descriptive \(e\.g\., lastLogin, savedPositions\)\.

## Data Integrity and Constraints

• __Unique Indexes__: Applied to email and roomCode\.  
• __Atomic Updates__: Uses $addToSet and $inc for room membership and stats\.  
• __Self\-healing__: The room list logic automatically fixes legacy data inconsistencies during retrieval\.
